clue.text: Passing in van, sharing time with politician

parts.note: a Transit is the Ford van ubiquitous on British roads

indicators.note: the van and the politician share their common letter for time, so it appears only once where they overlap

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Someone passing by in a van, sharing the ride with a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sharing' means the van and the politician overlap on their one common letter for time, which is written once. 'Passing' reads as driving by, but means fleeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something passing lasts only a short while; the two words are synonyms meaning fleeting.

clue.text: Drawn, having temperature, looking rough with no resistance

indicators.note: with no tells us the letter for resistance is taken away from the rough-looking word

parts.note: rugged describes a rough, weathered look
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone looking drawn, feverish and rough, with no fight left in them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawn' suggests a haggard face, but here it is the past tense of draw, meaning pulled.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawn as in pulled along: a rope that has been drawn has been pulled hard, a synonym.

clue.text: Dish out a dose of own medicine in Whitehaven General?

definitions.text: Dish out a dose of own medicine

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words Whitehaven General, running across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A hospital, Whitehaven General, dishing out a dose of its own medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitehaven is a town in Cumbria, so Whitehaven General reads as its hospital, which fits the medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a dose of their own medicine is to pay back a wrong in kind, which is retaliation.

clue.text: I spill mystical liquid in a shallow way

indicators.note: liquid suggests something flowing and shapeless, so the letters run into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone confessing they spill a mystical potion, done in a shallow way.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in an oversimplified manner that ignores complexity, so lacking depth or shallow.

clue.text: Person responsible for notes in tango decided to interrupt final section

parts.note: T is Tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: to interrupt means to break into the middle of the final section

parts.note: the rear is the last part of something
sure means certain, decided in mind

explanation.surface: A dancer, decided in the tango, interrupts the final section of the performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' suggests music to go with the tango, but they are banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: A club or company officer keeps the money, banknotes included, so manages the funds.

clue.text: Drinks stout

definitions.meaning: a set of drinks bought for the whole group, as in 'my shout'
stout as an adjective, meaning plump and rotund

explanation.surface: Ordering drinks of stout, the dark beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Stout looks like the beer to go with the drinks; it is the adjective for plump.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinks order for everyone at a pub table, and also a plump, rotund figure.

clue.text: Likelihood one in ounces could be seen as this?

definitions.text: Likelihood one in ounces could be seen as this?

parts.words: Likelihood one in ounces could be seen as this?
parts.note: chances are given as 'one in' so many; and in the word ounces the O, read as one, is an odd one, so these are betting chances

explanation.surface: A question about the chance of something being one in a number of ounces.
explanation.walkthrough: Chance is often given as one in so many, and betting prices are quoted the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookmakers' prices express probability, the chance of something happening.

clue.text: Log jam six feet under part of canal

parts.note: six feet under is an idiom for buried, so not alive
a lock is the gated chamber that raises and lowers boats on a canal

explanation.surface: A log jam sitting deep beneath part of a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Log jam' looks like timber blocking the canal, but here it means a standoff.
explanation.definitionFit: A log jam is figuratively a stalemate in which no side can move forward.

clue.text: In haste, parking to enter in scruffy style

indicators.note: to enter says the parking letter goes inside the scruffy-style word

parts.note: seedily means in a shabby, run-down way
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Someone hurriedly parking and going inside, dressed in a scruffy style.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in haste means done quickly, at a swift pace.

clue.text: A condiment more 'runny' — good word!

indicators.note: runny describes something that flows freely and loses its shape, so the letters run into a new order

explanation.surface: A condiment that is more runny, praised with a good word.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting in a good word for someone is a favourable endorsement or reference.

clue.text: Flash Seventies rock style involving energy

indicators.note: involving means the rock style wraps around the energy letter

parts.note: glam rock was the glittery 1970s style of Bowie and T. Rex
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Flashy glam rock of the Seventies, full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flash' looks like an adjective for showy, fitting glam, but it is a noun meaning a brief light.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief shine or glint of light, as in a gleam in the eye.

clue.text: List in menu revamped before the Queen dined

indicators.note: before puts the reworked menu ahead of the following pieces
revamped means remade, so the letters of menu are reordered

parts.note: ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina
ate is the past tense of eat, meaning dined

explanation.surface: A list on a revamped menu shown before the Queen dined.
explanation.definitionFit: To list items is to name them one by one, counting them off in order.

clue.text: Apparently forces to be located in Middle Eastern area swamps

indicators.note: apparently means seemingly, so the letters are what the phrase seems to be when spoken

parts.words: forces to be located in Middle Eastern area
parts.note: troops stationed in the Gulf, the Persian Gulf region, could be described as 'in Gulfs'

explanation.surface: Forces seemingly to be stationed in the Middle East, swamped by events.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gulf is the Persian Gulf; forces posted 'in Gulfs' said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Swamps as a verb, meaning floods over and overwhelms completely.

clue.text: Did sketch in which party facing both ways governed

indicators.note: facing both ways means the party word is written forwards and then turned back on itself

parts.note: a do is a party, written once forwards and once backwards
led means directed or governed

explanation.surface: A cartoonist sketching a party that faced both ways while it governed.
explanation.definitionFit: To doodle is to draw idle little scribbles, a casual kind of sketching.

clue.text: Tremendous macaroni — lots to be used

indicators.note: to be used means put to work and remade, so the letters of macaroni and lots are reordered

explanation.surface: A tremendous amount of macaroni, with lots to be eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomical means huge, as in sums of the size of distances in space.

clue.text: Boy used up scented stuff around girl, getting half-cut and sentimental

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, so the boy word is turned around

parts.note: a son is a boy

indicators.note: around says the scented stuff wraps around the half girl

parts.note: talc is scented talcum powder

indicators.note: half-cut means only the first half of girl is kept

explanation.surface: A boy used up scented powder around a girl, getting tipsy and sentimental.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British slang for drunk, which makes the surface; here it halves girl to GI.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentimental about the past, wistfully longing for earlier times.

clue.text: Ready for romance, very modern

parts.note: up to as in 'up to the job', meaning ready for or capable of
a date is a romantic outing

explanation.surface: Someone ready for romance, being very modern about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Current with the latest trends and information, the latest in fashion.

clue.text: Blessed drips from the ministry

parts.note: water sprinkled by a minister during a christening ceremony; drips sounds like feeble people from a government ministry

explanation.surface: Pious wets coming out of a government ministry.
explanation.definitionFit: Christening ceremonies, where clergy sprinkle holy water on a child.

clue.text: Copying letter from Greece will limit delay occurring

indicators.note: will limit means the Greek letter hems in the delay on both sides

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a lag is a delay
arising means coming about, occurring

explanation.surface: A letter from Greece limits a delay that keeps occurring.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing off someone else's writing as one's own is copying it.

clue.text: Country person wasting no time in conversation?

indicators.note: in conversation means as heard when spoken, the question mark flagging the loose match

parts.note: a rusher is someone who hurries

explanation.surface: A country person who wastes no time in chatting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country person' reads as one phrase, a rustic; 'Country' is the definition alone. The match works in non-rhotic British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia is the largest country in the world by area.

clue.text: Amid first set, Edberg, going head over heels, can't stand

indicators.note: head over heels means turned upside down, so in a down clue the run is read upwards
amid says the letters sit inside the words first set, Edberg

explanation.surface: Edberg, tumbling during the first set, can't stand.
explanation.walkthrough: Stefan Edberg was a Swedish tennis champion. The letters TSETED inside the words are turned around.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something is to be unable to bear it.

clue.text: Bans unfashionable boys in blue Sierra

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
the boys in blue are the police, the law
S is Sierra in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Unfashionable policemen in a Sierra, the old Ford car, get banned.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sierra was a popular 1980s Ford saloon car.
explanation.definitionFit: To ban something is to make it illegal, prohibiting it by law.

clue.text: Drop that's put under the microscope

definitions.meaning: a fall or decline, as in a drop in prices
a glass plate holding a specimen for examination

explanation.surface: A drop of liquid placed under a microscope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop' suggests a droplet for the microscope; it means a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a fall in value and the glass mount for a microscope sample.

clue.text: Group of motorists keeping small lead in the main

indicators.note: keeping means holding the small letter inside the motorists' group

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
to rule is to lead or govern

explanation.surface: A motoring organisation keeping a small lead in the main.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's Automobile Association, which rescues broken-down drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: In the main means generally, usually, for the most part.

clue.text: Tar perhaps filling in this clearing

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, as is an AB, an able-bodied seaman
what the solver does with this crossword is work it out

explanation.surface: Tar being used to fill in a clearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tar' looks like the road material for filling, but it is a sailor; 'this' is the crossword itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearing someone of blame means pardoning them, freeing them from guilt.

clue.text: Problem children

definitions.meaning: a matter in dispute, a topic of concern
offspring, as in dying without offspring

explanation.surface: Children who are a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a point of difficulty and, in legal language, a person's offspring.

clue.text: Not rocket science, returning post-ready envelope with address unknown

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the envelope abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: an SAE is a stamped addressed envelope, ready for posting
Y is an algebraic unknown, as in x and y

explanation.surface: Returning an envelope ready for posting, but the address is unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address unknown' looks like a postal phrase, but address belongs with the envelope and unknown stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is not rocket science is simple, needing little effort.

clue.text: Later family member finds insect beside sink

indicators.note: beside places the insect next to the sink word

parts.note: to descend is to go down, to sink
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A family member finds an insect beside the kitchen sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sink' looks like the kitchen fixture; it is the verb for going down.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring of a later generation, such as a grandchild, in a family line.
